Recommendation: Do not remove or soften explicit content to qualify for the French Top 50.
Supporting evidence: 56.3% of rows and 62.4% of the Top 10 are explicit; explicit Top 10 rate 22.2% vs 17.2% clean.

Recommendation: Aim for roughly 2.5-4 minutes; treat tracks over 4 minutes as a risk to Top 10 presence.
Supporting evidence: Medium = 84.9% of Top 10 vs 81.7% overall; Long = 3.7% vs 5.4%.

Recommendation: Lead with singles or clear focus tracks when popularity and Top 10 entry are the goal; albums remain viable.
Supporting evidence: Singles: popularity 80.8 vs 73.3 (robust at track level); rank advantage modest and not robust.

Recommendation: Keep a clean version available as a low-cost complement to an explicit release.
Supporting evidence: Clean rows have higher popularity (80.9 vs 73.6) but not better chart positions; the data cannot show whether adding a clean version helps the same song.

Recommendation: Pitch both explicit and clean material; emphasise single-led, medium-length tracks for the top positions.
Supporting evidence: Top 10 is 50.8% single and 84.9% medium length; differences are moderate.

Recommendation: For album projects, concentrate promotion on a few focus tracks rather than the whole tracklist.
Supporting evidence: Album Size Impact Index -0.230 overall, -0.088 within albums only (weak); correlation, not causation.

Recommendation: Use this analysis as the French baseline and compare it with other markets before localising.
Supporting evidence: Only the France playlist is analysed; genre, language and artist origin are not in the data.
